## Splashdown Example

This example usage of VIRGO is inspired by `SIM_splashdown` from [the Trick repository](https://github.com/nasa/trick/tree/master/trick_sims/SIM_splashdown) and actually uses data generated from the sim which has been copied here to `log_splashdown.csv`. 

* `log_splashdown.csv`: Tracked Trickpy-compliant data file generated by Trick's `SIM_splashdown`.
* `scene.yml`: YAML scene file representing the `dict` VIRGO needs to build the 3D scene
* `splashdown.py`: Script that launches VIRGO using `scene.yml` and `log_splashdown.csv`
* `capsule.py`: AI-generated script that created `capsule.stl`, included here for completeness.

In this example a common spacecraft re-entry capsule shaped object is dropped from a still position at a 120 degree rotation and the physics of the drop and interaction with still water is modeled.  In addition to the motion of the capsule itself, VIRGO is configured to visualize the center of buoyancy as a frame that moves in inertial space  - press `L` to enable labels and see the `CoB` label name follow this frame.  Note that the `log_splashdown.csv` data file articulates the location of the `CoB` frame as co-located with the origin of the capsule if none of the capsule is submerged yet - this is how `SIM_splashdown` chooses to model it.

### Keep in Mind

Noting here some key differences between the true `SIM_splashdown` and this VIRGO representation of it.

1. `log_splashdown.csv` was generated by Trick's `SIM_splashdown` in December 2025 which could differ from that same SIM run tdoay. Furthermore this file has been slightly altered from the original Trick sim generated file, mostly to transpose the `R[0-2][0-3]` matrix as the sim records it as body-to-world but VIRGO needs it in world-to-body. Ideally the simulation would be altered to present `R` (or another named recorded variable) in the correct frame VIRGO needs, this was just a quick path towards providing an example here.
2. The geometry provided by `capsule.stl` and sized by `scene.yml`'s `actors: capsule: scale:` does not perfectly match the geometry defined in `SIM_splashdown` and `scale:` was configured by eye to "look right" but no further verification was done regarding accuracy of `capsule.stl`. The path was chosen because the simulation itself has geometry hardcoded in C++ files in a way that VIRGO cannot consume, so this example provides a similar (but not exactly correct) geometry in `capsule.stl` generated by `capsule.py`.
